lesson_title: A Town That Breathes: Business Cycles
hook_text: Every economy breathes in and out. The trick is knowing which breath you're in.
clip_script: Take a coastal town that lives on tourists. Season one: guesthouses half-empty, waiters on short shifts. Nothing getting worse — just flat. That's the TROUGH. Then a good December gets booked. The guesthouse hires two cleaners, the restaurant orders more fish, the builder starts four new rooms. Those wages hit the spaza, those takings get spent again — the town climbs month after month. UPSWING. Then the town is FULL. Every bed taken, prices creeping up, not one spare bricklayer at any wage. PEAK — the town cannot do more. Then petrol jumps, or the road floods, or visitors just feel poorer. Bookings thin, a cleaner is let go, her spending vanishes from the spaza. Each loss causes the next. DOWNSWING — until it flattens into a new trough. That's a business cycle: trough, upswing, peak, downswing, riding on a slow upward slope called the trend. And here's the exam gold: somebody leans against the wave. The Reserve Bank turns the repo rate down when the town is cold — 2020 — and up when prices run — 2022. Not to punish you. To keep the breathing steady.
visual_style: One seaside main street cycling through four seasons in continuous time-lapse: empty stoeps filling with tourists, scaffolding rising, a FULL sign glowing, then shutters closing — while a wave-line traces the town's pulse above the rooftops.
mood: Warm and observational, sharpening into clarity.
pacing: Slow at the trough, accelerating through the upswing, a held beat at the peak, tumbling through the downswing, steady close.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and label any economy's phase — plus the policy answer — in one line.
